top.title: Fixtures and standings as Nations Championship returns
top.description: The Nations Championship resumed on Friday with Ireland securing a 42-12 win over Argentina, as the battle for continental supremacy heats up. After three rounds of home games for southern hemisphere nations in July, the northern hemisphere teams are the hosts for the final three rounds. Ireland's win moved them top of the northern standings until France thrashed Fiji 54-17 on Saturday to regain their lead with 17 points from four matches. Scotland were outclassed by New Zealand in the second half and are in third place in the northern table following a 43-21 defeat at Murrayfield. Fourth-placed England have 10 points and play Australia - who are third in the southern standings - at Allianz Stadium on Sunday. Wales overcame Japan 28-21 to move level on points with England but have a vastly inferior points difference. Bottom-side Italy, who lost all three of their away games in the summer, were outgunned 66-7 by South Africa on Saturday. The Springboks continue to lead New Zealand on points difference, with both teams having won all four of their games with bonus points. The world champions face Six Nations champions France in a huge game in Paris on Friday. The Nations Championship pits the northern hemisphere teams who compete in the Six Nations - England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, France and Italy - against southern hemisphere giants South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina, plus invited sides Fiji and Japan. All teams will play each of the six in the opposing hemisphere once, with three rounds of fixtures staged in July and another three in November. Their results will rank the teams within their own hemisphere, from one to six. On the final weekend in November, there is a three-day play-off event staged at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. The sixth-placed team in the northern hemisphere plays off against the equivalent in the southern hemisphere standings and so on, culminating in the two top-ranked sides taking each other on. The winner of that final match is crowned the inaugural Nations Championship winner. There is also a parallel, Ryder-Cup style hemisphere title. top.title: Jordan Love, Drake Maye represent new era in Packers-Patriots matchup
top.description: The Green Bay Packers and New England Patriots don’t play each other that often. The most recent time was in 2022, an overtime game at Lambeau Field won by Green Bay with Aaron Rodgers under center during his final season in Green Bay. In the teams’ most recent matchup in New England in 2018, Tom Brady was on the field playing in his penultimate season with the team. Sunday’s game between the Packers (5-3) and Patriots (5-3) won’t feature either future Hall of Famer. Rodgers is playing what he’s said is his final NFL season in Pittsburgh, and Brady will be calling his first game in Gillette Stadium as an analyst for Fox Sports. “I think I’m required contractually to catch up with him at some point,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel joked this week about Brady’s latest return to New England. But there will be plenty of focus on the quarterbacks that have come behind Rodgers and Brady for their respective former franchises. Jordan Love appears to be finding his stride in his fourth season as the full-time starter, leading the league in passing yards for a team looking to make the playoffs for the fourth consecutive season. Meanwhile, Drake Maye has recovered from a rough start to account for at least three touchdowns in each of his past five games, leading the Patriots to victories in four of them. While the Packers enter the game last in the NFL in rushing, averaging only 60.6 yards per game, Love said he isn’t worried about generating offense. “The run game isn’t where it needs to be, but I think we’ve still been able to kind of adjust and still make plays,” he said. “There’s a lot more out there, but we’ve done a great job just being able to win these games by putting up some points, and that’s what it comes down to.” Maye said the matchup is certainly a measuring stick opposite a team that like them is trying to keep pace in their division. “They’re good, they’ve beaten good teams, and they continue to show up every year,” Maye said. “We’ve definitely got a challenge and a chance to see how we look.” Need to know Green Bay (5-3) at New England (5-3) When/where to watch: Sunday, 4:25 p.m. EST, FOX. The Packers quarterback is leading the NFL with 2,246 passing yards (280.8 per game) to go along with 16 touchdown passes (fourth in the NFL). top.title: What activating Mack Hollins means for the Patriots
top.description: The writing was on the wall, and on Saturday the New England Patriots made it official. Mack Hollins has returned to the team’s 53-man roster after spending the previous four weeks on its injured reserve list; the veteran wide receiver was sent there after sustaining a calf injury in Week 4 versus the Buffalo Bills. Let’s assess what Hollins’ activation means for the Patriots ahead of their Week 9 contest versus the Green Bay Packers. Better depth Despite returning to practice earlier this week to open his 21-day window to return from injured reserve, Hollins initially remained on the list. While this is standard procedure — teams want to take a look at players at practice first before making any decisions regarding activation — it did leave the Patriots potentially three top-level wide receivers short heading into the weekend. Romeo Doubs remains on IR with a shoulder injury, while A.J. Brown was ruled out for a second straight game due to a knee issue. Had Hollins missed Sunday’s game as well, Drake Maye’s supporting cast would again have looked suspect, particularly considering running back TreVeyon Henderson’s medical status and tight end Hunter Henry being questionable for the contest as well. Hollins cannot patch all of those holes by himself, but having him available does upgrade New England’s overall defensive depth. Roster shakeup With Hollins back on the 53-man team, the Patriots now have five wide receivers rostered . In addition, their practice squad features three wideouts — one of whom, Ryan Miller, was elevated to the game day roster against the Miami Dolphins last week. 53-man roster (5): A.J. Brown (1), Mack Hollins (13), DeMario Douglas (3), Kyle Williams (18 | KR), Efton Chism III (86) Practice squad: Kyle Dixon (83), Chandler Brayboy (81), Ryan Miller (11) Injured reserve: Romeo Doubs (87) On paper, the Patriots are nearing full strength at the position again. That is particularly true given that Doubs will be eligible to come off IR himself after New England’s trip to Germany next week. The expectation is that he too will rejoin the active roster sooner rather than later, giving the club a full complement of wideouts again. That said, A.J. Brown’s status remains a question mark. While the team is optimistic that he will return before the end of the month, his participation in the upcoming international game against the Detroit Lions is uncertain. Trickle-down effect After Hollins exited the game against the Bills, one player in particular took on a bigger role: second-year man Efton Chism. top.title: Nebraska HC Matt Rhule has suffered losing streak since appearing on HBO hit Lanterns
top.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule made an appearance as himself on HBO and DC Studios’ show Lanterns last month, but his record since then hasn’t been great. Rhule played himself in the hit show, making an appearance in the final episode of the season while trying to recruit a character on the show. However, this one-time appearance in Hollywood may have jinxed his Cornhuskers, who haven’t been able to win a game since his cameo. Nebraska Cornhuskers go 0-4 after Matt Rhule’s appearance on HBO’s Lanterns After their latest loss to Illinois, one fan on social media pointed out that the Nebraska Cornhuskers have lost four games straight since Matt Rhule made an appearance on HBO and DC Studios’ hit show. In the show, Matt Rhule is there to help recruit Noah Macon to Nebraska as their next quarterback, not knowing that he was a half-alien being known as a manhunter. Macon, who was initially portrayed as a possible future villain, tells John Stewart that he wishes to lead a normal life and not fulfil his programming’s goal to take over humanity. In the canon of the DC Universe, Matt Rhule is pivotal to the future safety of the human race, as he will be one of the figures guiding and mentoring a manhunter with the power to take over the entire planet. However, that will come as little relief to Rhule and the rest of the Cornhuskers, given their woes this season. After their loss to Illinois, Rhule decided to fire OC Dana Holgerson, marking the first major personnel change he and the Cornhuskers have had to make. The Cornhuskers are currently 5-4 for the season, squandering what had been a solid 5-0 start to the season over the last month. Within the Big Ten, the Cornhuskers are 2-4, showing that they are far from being able to compete against the best of the best in their conference. top.title: Hashim raises alarm over 3.68m IDPs, insecurity before US commission
top.description: ABUJA — Accord Party presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has drawn the attention of the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) to Nigeria’s estimated 3.68 million internally displaced persons (IDPs), calling for greater international intervention over insecurity, religious persecution and ethnic discrimination. Hashim also called for the release of Hausa cultural activist, Maisango, whom he alleged was being unlawfully detained, and urged the international community to investigate reports of attacks and the burning of 11 villages in Shanga Local Government Area of Kebbi State. He made the appeal during an engagement with the commission on Friday, where he discussed Nigeria’s religious freedom and humanitarian challenges. According to a statement on the engagement, Hashim acknowledged that Christians in Northern Nigeria face persecution but argued that religious freedom violations also affect Muslim minorities, including Shia Muslims and Hausa communities. He said Nigeria’s religious freedom challenges extended beyond the conventional Christian-Muslim divide, alleging that ethnic identity and cultural affiliation also influenced religious and social acceptance in some communities. The Accord candidate particularly raised concerns about what he described as the marginalisation of Hausa Muslims in parts of Northern Nigeria, arguing that some communities experience unequal treatment despite sharing the same Islamic faith with other groups. On Maisango’s detention, Hashim alleged that the cultural activist had been held without trial despite reportedly being dismissed from his employment with the Department of State Services (DSS). He called for his immediate release, emphasising the need to respect due process and fundamental human rights. Hashim also cited an estimated 3.68 million internally displaced persons in Nigeria, referencing UNHCR figures as of October 2026, and argued that the humanitarian crisis cut across religious and ethnic boundaries. He specifically highlighted reported attacks on communities in Shanga Local Government Area of Kebbi State, including Kalkami, Tungar Bori and Kawara. According to him, reports of attacks in April 2026 indicated that suspected bandits killed residents, set buildings ablaze and forced inhabitants to flee their homes. He said reports that 11 villages were burnt in the area deserved sustained international attention. Hashim further alleged that some armed groups operating in the region were more interested in killing residents, destroying settlements and taking control of territory than in religious conversion. He blamed what he described as the government’s failure to adequately protect vulnerable communities and decisively confront armed groups, warning that the country’s security and religious freedom challenges must not deteriorate further ahead of another political transition. top.title: Today in White Sox History: November 8
top.description: Joe Nossek, who did a little bit of everything during two coaching tenures with the White Sox, was born on this day, 86 years ago. | (Photo by Ron Vesely/Getty Images) 1920 For a few days, the White Sox were members of the National League. With many owners dissatisfied with the National Agreement (governing the game, the majors, the minors, and all baseball commerce), 11 clubs hatched a plan to form a new National League — a single league including every team. Included in this “Allied Eleven” were the White Sox. With all 16 MLB teams gathering at the Congress Hotel in Chicago, the “Allied Eleven” met in one room and “Loyal Five” (to the American League, consisting of Cleveland, Detroit, the Philadelphia A’s, St. Louis Browns and Washington) another, with Senators owner Clark Griffith shuttling between the two rooms as messenger. When agreement couldn’t be struck to keep the AL-NL MLB dynamic going, the White Sox, Yankees and Red Sox all resigned from the AL and joined the National League. Cooler heads prevailed four days later, with the leagues remaining intact and the approval of Kenesaw Landis as baseball’s first commissioner was a key part of a redrawn National Agreement. The decisions and changes made at these 1920 meetings largely define the structure of baseball today, more than 100 years later. 1940 Joe Nossek , longtime White Sox coach over two stints in Chicago, was born, in Cleveland. He first joined Tony La Russa’s staff from 1984 to 1986, and returned for a much longer stint that represented his last work in the majors, from 1991-2003. Nossek was a bench coach during some of his second tenure with the White Sox, but was known as an “eye in the sky” coach, specializing in stealing signs from opponents. Nossek honed his bird-dogging skills as a seven-year outfielder in the majors, suiting up for the Twins, A’s and Cardinals. 1977 The upstart South Side Hit Men, who led the AL West for about a third of the season and took baseball by storm in peaking at 25 games better than .500, were laid to rest with the loss of outfielder and folk hero Richie Zisk , who signed a 10-year, $2.3 million deal with the Texas Rangers . Zisk was the lone All-Star for the White Sox in 1977, finishing seventh on the club with 2.7 WAR, and fifth among hitters. His 30 home runs were second on the team; among them one ball on the Comiskey Park roof and another in its center field bleachers, rare feats both. Zisk duplicated his All-Star selection in Texas in 1978, but never again came close to the production he put up for the White Sox. He was out of baseball with four seasons still remaining on his contract. Losing Zisk spotlighted the down side of owner Bill Veeck ’s desperate Rent-a-Player concept, as star relievers Terry Forster and Goose Gossage had been shipped out to secure just one year of the slugger. 1999 South Carolina Rep. top.title: Rory McIlroy comments on Patrick Reed and Eugenio Chacarra when asked about Race to Dubai chances
top.description: Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Rory McIlroy finished in third place this week at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, keeping his outside chances of winning the Race to Dubai for an eighth time alive. McIlroy played some exceptional golf this week at Yas Links, but he was far too inconsistent to challenge Jon Rahm in the end. The Northern Irishman made 29 birdies and one eagle in Abu Dhabi, but he also made a quadruple bogey, a double bogey and six bogeys. Rory McIlroy is still in with a shout of winning the Race to Dubai and he will be in the final group out alongside Eugenio Chacarra at The 2026 DP World Tour Championship on Thursday. He leap-frogged Patrick Reed into second place in the standings this week. And the six-time major champion has now opened up on how he feels about his chances of winning the season-long race next week in Dubai. Rory McIlroy comments on Patrick Reed and Eugenio Chacarra when asked about Race to Dubai McIlroy spoke to reporters after his final round in Abu Dhabi on Sunday. The Northern Irishman was asked whether he is content with his position in the Race to Dubai standings heading into the final event of the season next week in Dubai. “ Yeah, absolutely. That’s where I wanted to be, “ McIlroy replied. “ It’s a pretty familiar spot for me going into The DP World Tour Championship, and I’m excited for it. That was the goal coming into these two weeks to try to catch Eugenio and Patrick and try to win The Race to Dubai again. “ Yeah, it would have been great to win this week and give myself not as much of a deficit or even a lead, but I still feel like I’m right in there with a great chance. “ McIlroy then delivered his verdict on his performance this week at Yas Links. “ It was sort of a week where I felt like I had my chances, “ he admitted. “ You know, especially today, birdieing 10 and 11 on the back to get tied for the lead, and then I had two good chances, 12 and 13, and didn’t make those. Had to scramble for par on 14. And then, yeah, I just couldn’t keep my momentum going. “ But it was a good week. I saw some encouraging signs in the game. You know, I’m going to be in that final group going out on Thursday next week. So yeah, I obviously would have loved to have won the tournament, but enough positive signs to feel good about going into next week. “

top.title: NHL goalies from your nightmares: 5 all-time most frightening netminders in crease
top.description: Scoring a goal in the NHL is hard enough on any night. But going up against certain goalies was a total nightmare. These guys didn’t just stop pucks; they made the game feel like a street fight, messed with shooters’ heads and made players think twice before skating anywhere near the net. Some of them were straight-up bullies in the crease. If you got too close, you were getting slashed on the ankles, shoved or pulled into a brawl. Others relied on pure mind games, whether it was wearing creepy masks or using wild, unpredictable styles that made no sense but always worked. Just having them in net was enough to throw opposing players completely off their game. MORE: 3 NHL teams that should be worried after tough starts to 2026-27 season Best of all, they had the talent to back it up. They weren’t just goons in pads; they were champions. They lifted Stanley Cups, took home major awards, and came up with huge saves whenever their teams needed them. From bloody on-ice fights to mind-bending saves, these netminders left a serious mark on hockey history. Here are five goalies who truly terrified the players standing across from them. 5. Dominik Hasek: Unorthodox nightmare for shooters Buffalo Sabres goalie Dominik Hasek (39) on the ice against the New York Islanders at Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum. Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Dominik Hasek earned the nickname “The Dominator” by making saves that seemed impossible. His style looked chaotic compared with the techniques most NHL goalies use. He dropped his stick, rolled onto his back and threw his legs into the air to stop shots. For opposing forwards, predicting his next move was often a losing battle. Hašek’s numbers explain why his unusual approach worked so well. He recorded a career save percentage of .9223, the highest in NHL history among goaltenders who played more than 500 games. He also won the Vezina Trophy six times (1994, 1995, 1997, 1998, 1999 and 2001). The two-time Stanley Cup winner’s achievements went beyond goaltending awards. Hašek remains the only goalie in NHL history to win the Hart Memorial Trophy twice. His unpredictable saves and remarkable consistency made him a nightmare for even the league’s best scorers. 4. top.description: Red Sox Get Realistic Report on Chances of Landing Tarik Skubal originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Red Sox have needs on both sides of the baseball, but it's obvious that the front office is likely going to focus on the offensive side of things. If the Red Sox make the necessary moves during Major League Baseball's offseason, whether it be in free agency or the trade market, they should find themselves in a very good position to be one of the best teams not only in the American League but in all of baseball. Last season was somewhat difficult to evaluate for the Red Sox because at times they looked like one of the best teams in the game, but at other times they looked about average. There's obviously a lot of hope that the Red Sox will be that team day in and day out like they were for much of the big stretch a season ago, but that might be an unrealistic ask. Regardless, the easiest way to get there is to add players who can help them improve. At the top of that list would be Tarik Skubal, undoubtedly the best player on the free agent market. While Skubal would be a dream addition, the latest report suggests it's unlikely. “The Red Sox are likely to focus on improving their offense first and foremost, but there’s no such thing as too much pitching depth, so adding a middle-to-back-end starter is on the table. At the moment, the Red Sox possess a full rotation with Garrett Crochet, Ranger Suarez, Payton Tolle, Jake Bennett and Brayan Bello or Tanner Houck, but adding to that group will fortify against the inevitable injury. “While it’s not out of the question that the Red Sox try to reunite with Sonny Gray or target higher-end starters like Freddy Peralta or Trevor Rogers, it’s unlikely the Red Sox will be dropping $400 million to sign Tarik Skubal,” Jen McCaffrey wrote . A lot of this is going to come down to the type of money that Skubal will land on the free agency market. While the Red Sox could realistically give him that type of money, it doesn't make a whole lot of sense to pay one player $400 million when there are some needs on both sides of the baseball. I wouldn't hate the Red Sox landing Skubal because of how talented he is, but I also recognize it could create another hole that wouldn't be filled. top.title: Real Madrid youngster continues to impress Mourinho with outstanding all-round display against Valencia
top.description: Real Madrid youngster continues to impress Mourinho with outstanding all-round display against Valencia Real Madrid’s impressive resurgence under Jose Mourinho continued at Mestalla , with Los Blancos securing a 3-0 victory over Valencia. Mourinho’s men secured their eighth consecutive victory , with their performances improving with every passing game. Federico Valverde, Arda Guler and Kylian Mbappe scored the goals for Los Blancos , while Yan Diomande delivered another encouraging performance. According to MARCA (h/t RM4Arab ), the Ivorian’s growing defensive commitment has been particularly impressive as Mourinho continues to rely on him more and more. Diomande impresses with his defensive commitment One particular moment in the Valencia game underlined exactly how the 19-year-old can contribute to the team. Diomande sprinted nearly 30 metres to stop an opposition counter-attack. It was precisely the kind of effort Mourinho has been demanding from his attacking players. Yan Diomande has performed very well in Vinicius Jr.’s absence. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Diomande’s statistics were equally impressive. The youngster won 12 duels, completed six of his eight attempted dribbles, drew three fouls and succeeded in all three defensive tackles. He has now completed 37 dribbles in La Liga this season, placing him second behind Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal, who leads the standings with 43. His dribbling success rate of approximately 65% further demonstrates the consistency with which he has been troubling opposition defenders. Vinicius’ return presents Mourinho with a dilemma Diomande’s emergence has been particularly significant during Vinicius Junior’s four-match domestic suspension. The youngster has established himself as a serious option on the left wing at a time when the Brazilian is not in great form. How does Mourinho handle Vinicius’ minutes in the upcoming fixtures?. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Vinicius will be available for selection after the international break, having served his suspension. This leaves Jose Mourinho with an important decision over how to handle a superstar like Vinicius. The Portuguese manager could retain Diomande on the left or accommodate both players by moving the youngster to the opposite flank. What makes the situation especially interesting is that Diomande is increasingly offering more than attacking contributions. One of the biggest issues with Vinicius has been his reluctance to track back, and Mourinho’s team look more balanced with Diomande in it. It remains to be seen how Mourinho handles this situation and whether Diomande has done enough to displace Vinicius from the starting XI after the break.

top.title: Liverpool do not want to rush decision on Barcelona loanee despite talks over January move
top.description: Liverpool do not want to rush decision on Barcelona loanee despite talks over January move Ronald Araujo has been nothing short of a revelation in the Premier League, ever since his loan move to Liverpool in the summer. The Uruguayan international, often labelled as an error-prone defender, has fit in incredibly well at Anfield, notably becoming a regular starter in the right-back position. Araujo even won the Liverpool player of the month award in November , with many now believing that the Reds will trigger his €55 million buyout clause. Liverpool in no rush All eyes on Ronald Araujo’s progress at Liverpool. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images) However, a recent report from Diario SPORT has offered some updates on the future of Araujo. The report suggests Liverpool are in no hurry to make a decision as far as Araujo’s future is concerned. They do not want to activate the buyout clause just yet. The season is long, and the club are looking to wait until the latter part of the season before making any decision. As things stand, given the defender’s current form, Liverpool would be more than happy to pay €55 million to acquire the services of the on-loan Barcelona defender. This comes on the back of recent reports that suggest Liverpool have held talks with Barça over a potential January transfer for Araujo. It was suggested that the Reds were willing to activate the clause in the winter transfer window, but that is not the case, for now. Araujo aware of Barcelona interest Araujo is thriving in the Premier League. (Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images) Araujo, for his part, is also not thinking too much about his future at Liverpool for now and is focusing solely on his development. He knows that Barcelona are closely monitoring his progress. Given his affection for the club, one can be forgiven for thinking he would want to prove doubters wrong by coming back to Catalonia. Barcelona, for their part, could have used the services of Araujo given the club’s ongoing injury crisis in the defensive unit. That being said, it does seem likely that Araujo will be headed to Liverpool permanently next season. What remains to be seen is whether he can remain fit and continue his solid performances at the back.

The Accord candidate particularly raised concerns about what he described as the marginalisation of Hausa Muslims in parts of Northern Nigeria, arguing that some communities experience unequal treatment despite sharing the same Islamic faith with other groups. On Maisango’s detention, Hashim alleged that the cultural activist had been held without trial despite reportedly being dismissed from his employment with the Department of State Services (DSS). He called for his immediate release, emphasising the need to respect due process and fundamental human rights. nigeria.title: Bandits kill 12 family members, abduct others in Zamfara
nigeria.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Armed men suspected to be bandits have killed 12 members of the same family and abducted several residents during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. The attack reportedly occurred on Saturday night in Dosara Birnin Kaya Ward, with the assailants setting a room ablaze after the family members reportedly locked themselves inside to avoid being abducted. A source in the area told Vanguard that the victims belonged to the family of one Mallam Muhammadu Sani, who had gathered his relatives in a single room in an attempt to protect them from the attackers. According to the source, the bandits ordered the occupants to open the door but, after they refused, set fire around the room, killing all 12 family members. Several other residents were also reportedly abducted during the raid, although the exact number of those kidnapped could not be immediately ascertained. The 12 victims were buried on Sunday morning in accordance with Islamic rites. The attack comes amid recurring bandit attacks and security concerns along the busy Gusau-Sokoto road, where commuters have continued to face threats from armed criminals. Residents condemned the killings, describing the incident as barbaric, and called on security agencies and the Zamfara State Government to intensify efforts to protect lives and property. As of the time of filing this report, security agencies had yet to issue an official statement on the attack. nigeria.title: Court awards N50m damages against Pararan over defamation
nigeria.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi EFFURUN — A Delta State High Court sitting in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area, has awarded N50 million in damages against the proprietor of Pararan Mock News, Diamond Dietanuru Osakorigho, popularly known as Pararan, over a Facebook publication found to be defamatory against Apostle Michael Akpor. The court, presided over by Justice R.D. Harriman, also ordered Osakorigho to publish an unreserved apology to the cleric in Vanguard and The Nation newspapers within 14 days. It directed that the apology must enjoy the same prominence and circulation as the original publication. The judgment was delivered on November 6, 2026, in Suit No. EHC/91/2023. The court further restrained the defendant, his agents, privies, servants and all persons acting through him from publishing or causing to be published any further defamatory, injurious or libellous statements, videos or other materials against Akpor. It also awarded N1 million as costs of the suit. The case arose from a Facebook publication made on July 20, 2022, with the caption, “Warri Pastor Kpuf 2Keke passenger”, which the court found to be false and defamatory. Reacting to the judgment, counsel to the cleric, Austin Nyekigbe, a human rights activist, described the ruling as a significant statement on responsible social media engagement. He said the judgment reinforced the principle that freedom to use social media did not confer the right to publish false and defamatory information about others. “People must learn to verify information before rushing to publish it, particularly on social media. An injustice to one is an injustice to all,” he said. Also commenting on the judgment, a Warri-based lawyer, Mrs Eloho Avwaruroro-Okoye, who was present in court, said the decision underscored the legal consequences of irresponsible online publications. According to her, freedom of expression comes with responsibility, adding that those who publish false and damaging information must be prepared to face the legal consequences. She congratulated Akpor on his victory and commended Nyekigbe for his diligence in handling the case. The legal dispute followed allegations linking Akpor and two policemen attached to him to the July 12, 2022, killing of two persons at Ugbolokposo community in Effurun. However, Nyekigbe said police investigations subsequently exonerated his client and the two officers, identified as ASP Mesoro Victor and Inspector Ignatius Achazie. He said findings from the investigation, including witness statements, vehicle identification exercises and church CCTV footage, contradicted allegations linking the cleric to the killings. According to him, the police investigation report established that Akpor was at his church when the incident occurred, concluding that he was “going on with his religious business in the Church”. Nyekigbe, however, expressed sympathy with the families of the deceased. The post Court awards N50m damages against Pararan over defamation appeared first

nigeria.title: Troops neutralise suspected criminal, arrest five in Plateau
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Troops of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP) have neutralised a suspected notorious criminal in Wase Local Government Area and arrested five suspected phone snatchers during a raid on a hotel in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The operations also led to the recovery of 26 mobile phones and other items suspected to be stolen, including laptops, earpods and power banks. Military sources disclosed that the suspected criminal, identified as Abubakar Ango, was arrested on November 4 by troops of Sector 2 OPEP at Kukawa village in Wase. “At about 7:20 a.m. on November 6, during interrogation, the suspect reportedly confessed to involvement in several criminal activities and agreed to lead troops to his gang’s hideouts in a village forest,” the sources said. They explained that the mission was intended to facilitate the recovery of weapons and possible arrest of other members of the gang. “However, while being escorted to the location, the suspect allegedly attempted to seize the rifle of one of the soldiers, prompting an immediate response that resulted in his neutralisation,” they said. On the Jos operation, the sources said troops of Sector 1 OPEP arrested five suspected criminals during a raid on a Hotel along Baring Road in Jos North. “The troops, while on patrol, responded to a report of phone snatching at about 9 p.m. on November 6, 2026. The stolen phone was reportedly tracked to the Hotel within the area, prompting troops to conduct a raid on the facility,” the sources said. They disclosed that the five suspects were found in possession of the tracked phone, while a further search led to the recovery of 26 mobile phones, 27 pouches, three MP devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a knife and four power banks. “The vehicle belonging to the suspects was also towed to the headquarters of Sector 1 for a comprehensive search,” the sources added. “The suspects and recovered exhibits have been taken into custody for further investigation and necessary action,” the sources said. Confirming the two incidents, the spokesperson for Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Chinonso Oteh, urged residents to cooperate with the military and other security agencies by providing credible and timely information to assist ongoing operations. “We urge members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements and activities to security operatives,” Oteh said. He stressed that the cooperation of residents was critical to the success of ongoing efforts to combat criminal activities and restore lasting peace across Plateau State. “We assure residents of the military’s continued commitment to protecting lives and property and urge them not to hesitate to share useful information with security agencies,” he said. nigeria.title: Man returns home after 28-yr journey walking around the world
nigeria.description: A British adventurer, Karl Bushby, has returned to his childhood home in Hull, northern England, after completing a 28-year walking journey around the world that covered approximately 50,000 kilometres. Bushby, 57, was welcomed by his mother, Angela, outside her terraced house on Monday, November 2, 2026, beneath a banner reading “Welcome Home Son”. Hundreds of supporters had gathered in the city centre to celebrate his return before he completed the final stretch of his journey to his mother’s home. “Sorry to keep you waiting,” he joked to the cheering crowd. “Is that it, is it done?” Bushby began the expedition, known as the Goliath Expedition, in November 1998 in Punta Arenas, southern Chile. His goal was to travel around the world and return to his hometown without using any form of motorised transport to advance his journey. Carrying a tent, a few hundred dollars and a plastic camera, he initially expected the expedition to take about 12 years. His route took him north through the Americas before crossing the frozen Bering Strait from Alaska into Russia. He subsequently travelled through Mongolia and China, swam across the Caspian Sea and continued towards Europe. The journey also involved navigating the dense Darien Gap jungle between Colombia and Panama, crossing international borders and dealing with visa restrictions. Bushby was detained after entering Russia, while funding difficulties and the global financial crisis of 2008, which cost him major sponsors, contributed to delays that extended the expedition to 28 years. In the final stages of the journey, he swam across the English Channel last month, clearing one of the remaining major obstacles before walking the final distance to Hull. Speaking after his arrival, Bushby acknowledged the support he received from people and organisations across different countries. “They say it takes a village, but literally it took a world to get me here,” he said. “The kindness of strangers, so many, from individuals to nation-states, to get me back here today. I didn’t do this alone. There was a big team. The biggest team. Earth.” A feature-length documentary about his expedition is currently in production, while Bushby is expected to begin a speaking tour across England in the coming weeks. nigeria.title: Inuwa seeks common Northern policy framework to tackle out-of-school children
nigeria.description: Advocates unified regional agenda, investment in agriculture, agro-allied industries to combat poverty, insecurity Sultan applauds Gombe governor’s Almajiri education reforms By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe Gombe State Governor and Chairman of the Northern States Governors’ Forum, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has called for a common policy framework and unified regional agenda to sustain education reforms, tackle the growing number of out-of-school children and accelerate human capital development across Northern Nigeria. The governor said addressing the region’s educational challenges required a coordinated approach that went beyond school enrolment to include poverty reduction, improved security, economic empowerment and the creation of sustainable livelihood opportunities for the growing population. Yahaya made the call at the 2026 Biennial Lecture and Awards Ceremony of the Barewa Old Boys Association (BOBA), held in Gombe, with the theme, “The Scourge of Out-of-School Children and the Implications for National Security.” Describing the theme as timely and critical to the future of Northern Nigeria, the governor warned that the increasing number of children outside the formal education system posed serious threats to social stability, economic productivity and national security. He observed that educational exclusion perpetuated poverty, widened inequality and exposed vulnerable children and young people to criminal exploitation, radicalisation and other antisocial tendencies. Yahaya recalled that when his administration assumed office in 2019, Gombe State had more than 500,000 out-of-school children, explaining that sustained interventions by his government had brought approximately 350,000 of them back into the classroom. He attributed the achievement to the declaration of a state of emergency in the education sector, construction of mega schools with expanded learning capacities, recruitment of more than 1,000 qualified teachers and establishment of Almajiri Integrated Learning Centres, among other initiatives. Drawing from the state’s experience, the governor urged Northern states to move away from fragmented interventions and embrace a common regional framework that would identify successful educational models, encourage their adoption across state boundaries and guarantee continuity. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. sports.title: Fixtures and standings as Nations Championship returns
sports.description: The Nations Championship resumed on Friday with Ireland securing a 42-12 win over Argentina, as the battle for continental supremacy heats up. After three rounds of home games for southern hemisphere nations in July, the northern hemisphere teams are the hosts for the final three rounds. Ireland's win moved them top of the northern standings until France thrashed Fiji 54-17 on Saturday to regain their lead with 17 points from four matches. Scotland were outclassed by New Zealand in the second half and are in third place in the northern table following a 43-21 defeat at Murrayfield. Fourth-placed England have 10 points and play Australia - who are third in the southern standings - at Allianz Stadium on Sunday. Wales overcame Japan 28-21 to move level on points with England but have a vastly inferior points difference. Bottom-side Italy, who lost all three of their away games in the summer, were outgunned 66-7 by South Africa on Saturday. sports.description: The writing was on the wall, and on Saturday the New England Patriots made it official. Mack Hollins has returned to the team’s 53-man roster after spending the previous four weeks on its injured reserve list; the veteran wide receiver was sent there after sustaining a calf injury in Week 4 versus the Buffalo Bills. Let’s assess what Hollins’ activation means for the Patriots ahead of their Week 9 contest versus the Green Bay Packers. Better depth Despite returning to practice earlier this week to open his 21-day window to return from injured reserve, Hollins initially remained on the list. While this is standard procedure — teams want to take a look at players at practice first before making any decisions regarding activation — it did leave the Patriots potentially three top-level wide receivers short heading into the weekend. sports.title: Today in White Sox History: November 8
sports.description: Joe Nossek, who did a little bit of everything during two coaching tenures with the White Sox, was born on this day, 86 years ago. | (Photo by Ron Vesely/Getty Images) 1920 For a few days, the White Sox were members of the National League. With many owners dissatisfied with the National Agreement (governing the game, the majors, the minors, and all baseball commerce), 11 clubs hatched a plan to form a new National League — a single league including every team. Included in this “Allied Eleven” were the White Sox. With all 16 MLB teams gathering at the Congress Hotel in Chicago, the “Allied Eleven” met in one room and “Loyal Five” (to the American League, consisting of Cleveland, Detroit, the Philadelphia A’s, St. Louis Browns and Washington) another, with Senators owner Clark Griffith shuttling between the two rooms as messenger. When agreement couldn’t be struck to keep the AL-NL MLB dynamic going, the White Sox, Yankees and Red Sox all resigned from the AL and joined the National League. Cooler heads prevailed four days later, with the leagues remaining intact and the approval of Kenesaw Landis as baseball’s first commissioner was a key part of a redrawn National Agreement. The decisions and changes made at these 1920 meetings largely define the structure of baseball today, more than 100 years later. 1940 Joe Nossek , longtime White Sox coach over two stints in Chicago, was born, in Cleveland. He first joined Tony La Russa’s staff from 1984 to 1986, and returned for a much longer stint that represented his last work in the majors, from 1991-2003. Nossek was a bench coach during some of his second tenure with the White Sox, but was known as an “eye in the sky” coach, specializing in stealing signs from opponents. Nossek honed his bird-dogging skills as a seven-year outfielder in the majors, suiting up for the Twins, A’s and Cardinals. 1977 The upstart South Side Hit Men, who led the AL West for about a third of the season and took baseball by storm in peaking at 25 games better than .500, were laid to rest with the loss of outfielder and folk hero Richie Zisk , who signed a 10-year, $2.3 million deal with the Texas Rangers . Zisk was the lone All-Star for the White Sox in 1977, finishing seventh on the club with 2.7 WAR, and fifth among hitters. His 30 home runs were second on the team; among them one ball on the Comiskey Park roof and another in its center field bleachers, rare feats both. Zisk duplicated his All-Star selection in Texas in 1978, but never again came close to the production he put up for the White Sox. He was out of baseball with four seasons still remaining on his contract. technology.title: Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery
technology.description: Superconductors carry electricity without resistance, but most only work a few degrees above absolute zero. In the late 1980s, copper-based materials called cuprates were found to superconduct at higher temperatures—reachable with affordable liquid nitrogen. Yet nearly 40 years later, physicists still don't agree on why. In a recent Science study, a team of physicists led by Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University in the Netherlands has found some answers by listening to the faint electrical crackle of current flowing into a cuprate. The missing electrons Central to the mystery of cuprates’ high-temperature superconductivity is a strange state called the pseudogap. “The pseudogap is a phenomenon of missing electrons,” Allan said. Above the temperature at which cuprates become superconducting, some of their electrons seem to vanish—measurements find far fewer of them at the energies where they should be. “Everybody knows that from different probes, you see that there's these vanishing electrons, but nobody knows why,” Allan said. technology.title: Doom delivers five minutes of terminal violence on an IBM mainframe
technology.description: Can an IBM Z mainframe run Doom? Of course it can. The more interesting question is whether you can play it through a text terminal without ruining your eyesight. WND Software's browser demo connects to an IBM Z mainframe over SSH using its terminal emulator. Wojciech Graj's DOOM-ASCII supplies the text-based carnage, replacing conventional graphics with colored characters. There's no sound. It is, however, completely playable (although you might need to recalibrate your vision to work out what is going on, particularly with regard to distant objects). Sessions are limited to five minutes, with room for up to 50 simultaneous users, but we had no trouble getting in. ASCII also presented no issues once the game was in motion. This writer played the original shareware release on an Amstrad ALT386SX portable, so squinting at an indistinct demon felt reassuringly familiar. That Doom can be persuaded to run on an IBM Z mainframe is not particularly noteworthy. The code has turned up everywhere from databases to PCB designers . Even the humble Pi Pico was roped into the fun. Keeping the action playable through a text terminal is the more entertaining achievement. A year ago, an IBM consultant persuaded Doom to run on IBM Z and LinuxONE using VNC to bring the pixelated mayhem to life. Using a terminal emulator, while a neat demonstration of the capabilities of WND's software, is perhaps more an example of "because I can" masochism. It's undeniably an enjoyable way to burn through five minutes. No installation or login required – just a willingness to shoot at punctuation. ®

technology.title: Internet governance about to get its quadrennial stress test at ITU meeting
technology.description: The International Telecommunications Union (ITU) kicks off its quadrennial plenipotentiary on Monday, and internet governance organizations are bracing in case the event becomes a forum for nation-states to try to challenge their roles. The ITU is the United Nations' specialized agency for information and communication technologies, meaning its members are nation-states. The body's role is to facilitate international connectivity, which it does by managing radio spectrum, satellite orbits, and working on relevant technical standards. Its key standards are pervasive. ITU-T X.509 sets out the rules of public key infrastructure. ITU-T E.164 governs telephone numbers. ITU-T H.264 and 265 define the video codecs used for most online streams. The ITU's role is largely uncontested, yet its work gets very close to that of the organizations who work on technologies that make the internet work. Those bodies include the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF); the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), which oversees the domain name system; and the regional internet registries (RIRs), which manage IP addresses. The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) works on HTML, CSS, and accessibility. Governments participate in work at those internet governance bodies but are just one voice among many and can't override the consensus-driven decision-making process they use, under a system which has come to be known as the multi-stakeholder governance model. At a 2025 event called WSIS+20, the United Nations endorsed multi-stakeholder governance by deciding that its Internet Governance Forum (IGF) should become a permanent body. That decision effectively endorsed multi-stakeholder governance, and kept the ITU out of internet standards. Yet the IGF hasn't met since WSIS+20, so it is yet to start operating meaningfully as a permanent body. This year's ITU meeting is therefore a moment at which stakeholders can stress-test the delicate balance between the ITU, internet governance bodies, and the emerging IGF. Such a test could see ITU members try to have it pursue new fields that overlap with work performed by internet governance organizations. This has already happened before. China tried to have the ITU work on " New IP" – a major revision to internet protocol, a technology the IETF manages. In 2022, Russia and China backed a candidate for the ITU presidency who favored giving nations a stronger role in internet governance, potentialy by having the ITU take over some standards work. That candidate was not elected. Ahead of next week's meetings, the Internet Society published a background paper that declared it is "actively challenging proposals that could affect the Internet's underlying technical architecture or increase fragmentation, as well as those that could affect connectivity, particularly for remote, underserved, and unserved communities." science.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
science.description: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life. To aid in distinguishing between habitable and inhabited planets, planetary scientist Samantha Gilbert-Janizek of the University of California, Riverside, developed a model that simulates the evolution of a rocky planet without life. "The model can help us see how habitable but non-living planets might mimic living planets," Gilbert-Janizek, who was a PhD student at the University of Washington when the research was conducted, said in a statement. Gilbert-Janizek built upon a model previously developed by Washington’s Rory Barnes that simulated the core, mantle, and crust of a planet. This new model pushed the simulation two steps further by incorporating the surface and atmosphere of the planet as well. In all, the model simulates 19 properties of a rocky planet that are not related to life, including the amount of heat a planet receives from its star , the exchange of heat and chemicals from the core to the surface, and the outflow of certain gases from the subsurface. Gilbert-Janizek’s starting point was to simulate the development of Earth had life never arisen here, therefore providing a baseline with which to compare to exoplanets . She ran the simulation from the birth of Earth 4.5 billion years ago to 500 million years into the future. The result was a lifeless world, but one that still had oceans and an atmosphere. "When we interpret observations of an exoplanet’s atmosphere, this tool will help us determine the probability that what we observe indicates life on the surface," said Gilbert-Janizek. An illustration shows the landscape of a primordial Earth before life arose as lightning splits the skies (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) What makes the simulation especially useful is its plug-and-play nature. Researchers can simply apply the bulk properties of whichever planet they are studying to the model, and then just let it run. If the result is a planet with an atmosphere that matches what is detected spectroscopically by the James Webb Space Telescope or, in the future, the various extremely large 30-meter-plus ground-based telescopes or NASA’s planned Habitable Worlds Observatory , then we know that planet probably does not have life as we know it. science.description: NASA announced its 2025 Astronaut Candidate Class on Sept. 22, 2025, at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credit: NASA/Helen Arase Vargas NASA is looking for the explorers who will help write the next chapter of human spaceflight. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation of astronauts will train to operate on the lunar surface, live and work beyond Earth, and take on missions that will push the boundaries of human exploration farther than ever before. U.S. citizens interested in joining the astronaut corps have until 11:59 p.m. EST Thursday, Dec. 3, to submit their completed application materials at: https://go.nasa.gov/3WyvlQi “This is an extraordinary time to join NASA’s astronaut corps,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems and operations that will ultimately carry crews to Mars. Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage. NASA’s astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation. If you are ready to join that tradition, come help write the next chapter of humanity’s greatest adventure.” NASA expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training as the next class of astronaut candidates. “The window is open. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." science.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
science.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . Now this is podracing! The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious. Fast and furious, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ignores recent racing game trends and bets big on arcade-y vibes, uncomplicated controls, and a high skill ceiling that challenges you with extremely high speeds, tight turns, and unexpected interruptions as other drivers try to ruin your day. science.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
science.description: null NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. But the road from Artemis II's success to crewed lunar landings and, later, a permanent moon base will take a lot of launches of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket, Isaacman stressed. "You know, a lot of people, especially in the space community, start getting [into] if the landers are there or not. I don't really care about that right now. What I care about is that we are launching big rockets no less than once a year," he said. "I think that's imperative for NASA to be doing these deep-space human spaceflight missions right now," Isaacman added. "So, we had a great mission in April of '26. We will launch again in '27." That coming launch will be for Artemis III, a crewed mission to low Earth orbit that will test docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's private lunar landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. "We need to continue to exercise those muscles," he said, referring to SLS liftoffs. "And, honestly, once a year isn't great, either. I mean, I don't think we're going to get back to the early [space] shuttle days, you know, four missions a year.
